title: A market-data pipeline: feed → queue → strategy
summary: A producer thread parses raw feed lines into ticks and pushes them through a bounded blocking queue. The consumer runs a moving-average crossover strategy. This is producer–consumer from slides 204–208, as trading systems use it.

steps.title: Parse feed lines
hints: `std::stod(s, &used)` throws on garbage; check `used == s.size()` to reject trailing junk like `12.5x`.
Wrap the conversions in `try { ... } catch (...) { return std::nullopt; }`.

steps.title: Producer and consumer threads
hints: The producer is a `std::thread` that pushes parsed ticks, then calls `queue.close()`.
The calling thread pops with `while (auto t = queue.pop())` until the queue is closed and drained.
Only read the producer's counters after `join()`: join is a synchronisation point.

steps.title: SMA crossover strategy
hints: Keep, per symbol, a `std::deque<double>` of the last `slow` prices and the last sign of `fast SMA − slow SMA`.
Emit a signal only when the sign **changes** (not at the first comparison).
